tldr: A 3-hour beginner lab where participants add generative AI to Java applications with LangChain4j and Quarkus, covering prompts, RAG, MCP tools and agents.
summary: In this hands-on lab, Stéphane Philippart and Matthieu Vincent show that integrating AI into an application does not require a new language or stack. Participants stay in Java and work with popular frameworks including LangChain4j and Quarkus.

The lab walks through the main aspects of building generative AI applications: customising prompts, enriching models with your own data through RAG, calling local or remote tools via MCP, and creating agents. Attendees only need a laptop and a browser, since a fully configured development environment is provided through EasyLab.
keyPoints: Integrate AI models into Java applications without leaving the Java ecosystem.
Frameworks used include LangChain4j and Quarkus.
Topics: prompt customisation, RAG, tool calling through MCP, and agents.
Environment is provided through EasyLab; only a laptop and browser are needed.
takeaways: Start with LangChain4j in an existing Java project before considering a new stack.
watchIf: You are a Java developer new to generative AI and want a guided, practical first integration.
